desc: example.nix with the project's own pedantix.toml (formatter off)

files.pedantix.toml:
# repository-wide pedantix configuration

# Built-in presets provide base values ("nixos-module", "nixpkgs-package";
# This flake provides a few presets with defaults for nixos modules and
# packages. See presets/*.toml. Explicit settings below win over the preset.
# preset = "nixos-module"

# Base formatter: "nixfmt" (default), "alejandra", "nixpkgs-fmt", or "off"
formatter = "nixfmt"
# Alternatively any stdin -> stdout command; overrides `formatter`.
# Because this executes an arbitrary program, it is only honored from
# configs you name explicitly (--config, --config-toml, --set) and the
# global XDG config; in an auto-discovered config it requires running
# with --allow-formatter-command.
# formatter-command = ["nixfmt", "--width=100"]

# Run the base formatter before sorting, and again after sorting to
# normalize layout. Both default to true.
# format-before-sort = true
# format-after-sort = true

# Where inherits should be sorted: "first" (default), "sorted", or "last"
# sorted sorts them alphabetically, else they are at the very top/bottom
# inherit-placement = "front"

# Exact number of blank lines between the bindings of a file's top-level
# attribute set. Unset: keep the blank lines as-is -- reordered set will
# by default drop all spacing; set this (or [attrs] blank-lines) to restore
# top-level-blank-lines = 1

# How deep the spacing reaches: 1 (the default) is only the file's
# outermost set, 2 also covers the sets its bindings define and so ons.
# In flake.nix files, `inputs` and `outputs` always count as top-level sets.
# top-level-blank-lines-depth = 1

# Which lines should receive spacing: "multiline" (default), "all"
# "multiline": spacing for bindings whose text spans several lines,
# consecutive single-line are kept together
# "all": apply spacing to all bindings.
# top-level-blank-lines-mode = "multiline"

# top-level-blank-lines vs. [attrs] blank-lines:
#   top-level-blank-lines does NOT descend into function-call sets, and
#     treats a flake.nix `inputs`/`outputs` body as its own top-level set.
#   [attrs] blank-lines applies to every attrset the attrs rules match, at
#     any nesting depth, including sets in function call,
#     and can be targeted per path via [[overrides]].

# Every construct below ([args], [attrs], [lets], [inherits], [lists])
# accepts the same three keys:
#   sort  = true/false    -- whether to reorder at all
#   first = [...]         -- names that always come first, in the given order
#   last  = [...]         -- names that always come last, in the given order
# [attrs], [lets], and [inherits] additionally accept:
#   name-style            -- "preserve" (default) / "identifier" / "string";
#                            "identifier" unquotes names that are valid
#                            identifiers: `"a" = 1;` -> `a = 1;`
#                            "string" quotes every name instead
# [attrs] additionally accepts:
#   merge = true/false    -- merge bindings sharing their first attrpath
#                            component into one nested set (default false):
#                         `a.b = 1; a.c = 2;` -> `a = { b = 1; c = 2; };`
#   flatten = true/false  -- flatten a binding whose value is an attrset
#                            holding a single binding (default false):
#                         `a = { b = 1; };` -> `a.b = 1;`
#   blank-lines = N       -- number of blank lines between the set's bindings
#   blank-lines-mode      -- "multiline" (default) / "all" / "off"; "off"
#                            suppresses spacing entirely for matched paths.
#   blank-lines-depth = N -- see top-level-blank-line-depth; wrappers like
#                            functions and lets do not count as levels).

# sorting in arguments
[args]
first = ["self", "lib", "config", "pkgs"]
# "<defaulted>" stands for all args with a default value, e.g. `name ? value`
last = ["<defaulted>", "..."]

# Sorting in attribute sets
[attrs]
first = ["imports", "enable", "package"]

# Sorting inside let ... in blocks
[lets]
sort = true

# Sorting of inherit arguments
[inherits]
sort = true

# List elements can be sorted too, but list order can be relevant
# this is ideally used per path:
# [lists]
# sort = true

# Per-path overrides. `path` is a glob over dot-separated attribute paths:
# `*` matches exactly one component, `**` any number (including zero).
# Each override may set the partial rules (sort/first/last) of any
# construct: attrs, args, lets, inherits, lists.
# [[overrides]]
# path = "**.programs.git.settings.alias"
# attrs.sort = false
#
# [[overrides]]
# path = "**.systemd.services.*"
# attrs.first = ["description", "wantedBy"]
#
# [[overrides]]
# path = "**.environment.systemPackages"
# lists.sort = true
#
# [[overrides]]
# path = "flake-file.inputs"
# attrs.blank-lines = 1
